lodging: SF 10/2–10/6 → Monterey exactly one night 10/6–10/7 → Yosemite exactly two nights 10/7–10/9 → SF 10/9–10/12

A.title: Temporal Arbitrage Master
A.operating_architecture: Protect scarce openings and first-trip anchors, then spend optional budget only after recovery is funded.

recovery: Long hotel recovery before evening. Salesforce Park is only a free stroller-friendly recovery layer if already geographically useful; never detour for it.
decisions: Protect Ferry Building, Ferry Plaza Farmers Market, and the Oct 3 Latine Makers opening window. Keep Salesforce Park contextual and on-route only. Bay Lights stays energy-dependent.

recovery: Substantial midday hotel recovery; keep the afternoon Presidio / Crissy cluster compact.
decisions: Use the first practical Muir Woods reservation. Keep the weekend Golden Gate parking timing advantage. Battery Spencer is a must-see only when safe legal parking is immediately workable, wind is manageable, visibility is useful, and current access recheck passes.

recovery: Keep the North Beach lunch and family reset. Run the Wharf / Hyde corridor as a compact sequence; drop optional dwell before cutting recovery.
decisions: Protect Alcatraz and Chinatown. Fortune Cookie Factory is a short Chinatown micro-stop / snack. Keep PIER 39 sea lions and Ghirardelli Square + Aquatic Park as real must-see stops. Use Powell–Hyde as transport and experience; make Lombard a first-visit stop when the corridor is efficient. No paid Coit observation deck.

recovery: Protect a food / bathroom reset before the Aquarium. Keep Monterey exactly one night.
decisions: Run Point Lobos, Carmel-by-the-Sea / Carmel Beach, 17-Mile Drive + Lone Cypress, and the late Aquarium window. Old Fisherman’s Wharf is the natural evening / dinner layer. Bixby Creek Bridge remains Skip; do not detour south.

recovery: Arrival-day recovery is protected after the Monterey → Yosemite transfer; no checklist marathon.
decisions: Use the safest current corridor after checking fire, smoke, road, and access conditions. Tunnel View, Bridalveil Fall, and Cook’s Meadow are the protected reveal. Mariposa Grove is substitution-only; it never displaces Valley / Glacier priorities and is skipped when access or recovery is uncertain.

recovery: Substantial afternoon Valley recovery; Washburn Point and Valley View yield before Glacier Point.
decisions: Glacier Point is protected when Glacier Point Road, weather, and visibility permit. If road or view conditions are poor, use the safe open Yosemite Valley fallback and preserve the afternoon recovery.

recovery: Keep the final Yosemite morning, then take the easy Yosemite → SF transfer and recover at the SF hotel. Do not add an SF photo stop.
decisions: Protect a short Yosemite morning before the SF transfer. Family recovery and an easy arrival take priority over every SF photo opportunity.

recovery: Leave the afternoon open for SF recovery. JFK Promenade / central Golden Gate Park is a free, stroller-friendly, car-free outdoor layer only if the family wants a low-commitment same-cluster outing.
decisions: Protect Japanese Tea Garden and preserve San Francisco Botanical Garden. Keep recovery time open; JFK Promenade is optional same-cluster outdoor context, not a replacement checklist.

recovery: Keep a generous packing and recovery buffer after the scenic finale.
decisions: Lands End and Painted Ladies / Alamo Square are protected first-visit stops. Twin Peaks / Christmas Tree Point is a must when the view is worthwhile; move it within the SF window to the clearest safe visibility window, or skip without treating fog as an itinerary failure. Do not add another paid attraction.
